_note: All on-screen text. Keys are used by the code; edit the strings freely. A list means one line is picked at random.

intro.entrance: Behold! The lord of this manor arrives, and the shadows bow before him.
intro.after: ...It's a very small manor. For testing.

first: The sun. My oldest enemy. Second oldest, after stairs.
Ah. Daylight. Personally, on purpose, at me.
I am not squinting. This is my brooding face.

window.open: Curtains open. Sunlight gets in. Brave of me.
window.half: Half open. A compromise. Very mature.

door.inspect: The door leads out. I'm not ready for out.

sconce.lit: A candle. Someone keeps lighting these. I'm choosing not to ask who.
sconce.unlit: An unlit candle. Waiting for evening, like me.

fidget.cape: Don't look at me like that.
fidget.hair: It's meant to look like this.

debug.testDialogue: This is a test dialogue line. It stays on screen one second plus a third of a second per word.

menu.title: Paused
menu.navHint: Up/Down choose · E select · Esc close

greet: Good evening, {name}. Your tea will be along presently.
{name}. You're up early. Or late. I find it hard to tell, these days.
Welcome home, {name}. The house has been expecting you.
accepts: Quite so, {name}. I shall make a note.
smalltalk: The east wing is closed to visitors, sir. Has been since the... since the...
Mind the third stair, sir. It has opinions.
The house is very quiet tonight, sir. It usually is.
I polished the mirror in the hall, sir. It's very clean. Nobody is ever in it.
ambrose.repeat: I believe I mentioned that, sir.
ambrose.bat: Your bat form, sir. Shall I open a window?

ritual.table: The guests are running late again, sir.
ritual.clock: Nearly time, sir. It is always nearly time.
ritual.wall: Pardon me, sir. I'll take the usual way.

table.empty: A table for guests. Nobody's coming. I checked.
table.set: Someone set places for dinner. Fine china. For nobody.

clock.ticking: A grandfather clock. It ticks like it's judging me.
clock.stopped: It says nine o'clock. It's been saying that all night.

twins._note: The Twins chapter. Each line is {who: liam | twins | ambrose, face: portrait name, text}. Portraits - liam: grand smug flat startled panicked embarrassed soft sad; twins: stare tilt giggle whisper pout lonely delighted peace; ambrose: composed polite eyebrow drifting remembering concerned warm shaken.

ui.goHint: The nursery is down the landing.
ui.seekHint: Find the Twins. Press E on anything that could hide a small girl.
ui.batHint: Q: turn into a bat (and back). Now hide!
ui.learned: Learned: turn into a bat at will (Q)

bedroom.text: My room. Still bare. Minimalist. On purpose.

landing.text: Behold: the landing. Long. Dark. A great many doors.
I love it here. I'm lying.

guest.text: A guest room. For guests. I've never had one.

linen.text: A linen closet. Cosy. Or a trap. Cosy trap.

opening.text: It's Liam. And I can't drink tea.
Of course, sir. I shall leave it here regardless.
Oh, and sir. The young misses are rather lively this evening. In the nursery.

openingAfter.text: I don't have young misses. I don't have a nursery. ...I have a nursery?
Very well. I shall go and complain. Majestically.

landingBall.text: Balls do that. On slopes. This floor is flat. I checked. Just now. With my whole soul.

horse.text: The horse is rocking. Nobody is on the horse.

chest.text: And the toy chest is... knocking. From the inside.

after.text: You're not the one who was counting.
That was a tactical retreat. Bats are very tactical.

count.text: One. Two. Three. This is beneath me. Four...
...Nine. Ten. Ready or not, I suppose.

seekStart.text: I'm very good at finding things. I found this house. It was in a will.

teatable.text: My evening tea. Going cold. I can't drink it anyway. It's the thought that counts.

teatableLater.text: The tea's still there. So is the drawing. Things are piling up. In a nice way.

painting.text: A picture-book painting. Toy soldiers marching on a fort. Very wholesome. Suspiciously still.

paintingSeeking.text: The soldiers in the painting have moved. I'm almost sure the soldiers have moved.

bed2.text: It's a rag doll. It's a rag doll with one button eye. I'm fine.

bed2Later.text: The rag doll is watching me. With its remaining eye.

chest.text: Blocks. Tops. A jack-in-the-box with no jack. Nobody in it. Good. Great.

chestLater.text: The toy chest. Nothing in it but toys and my dignity.

horse.text: It's rocking again. I didn't touch it. I'm not touching it.

horseLater.text: The horse rocks whenever I look at it. I'll stop looking at it.

dollhouse.text: A dollhouse. It's this house. There's a tiny butler in the hall.

dollhouseLit.text: A light just went on in the dollhouse. Top floor.
Nobody up there. Nobody small enough, anyway.

marks.text: Height marks on the wainscot. Two, at the same height. Then nothing above them.

underbed.text: Under the bed: dust, one white ribbon, and two small footprints. Heading for the wardrobe.

curtainsScare.text: The curtains moved. Without me. That's my job.

linens.text: Sheets, folded with military precision. Ambrose.
Or something that folds like Ambrose.

wardrobeLater.text: The wardrobe. Two coats. They're not people. I checked twice.

tooBig.text: I don't fit in a wardrobe. I'd need to be smaller. Much smaller. With wings.

frida.text: You were under a quilt. You were a lump. I'm good at lumps.

wilhelmina.text: I was watching you the whole time.
Yes. I noticed the eye. Everyone noticed the eye.

oneLeft.text: One down. One small, unblinking one to go.

both.text: Both found. They want me back in the nursery. To play 'properly'.

yourTurn.text: Hide. Where? I'm taller than every hiding place in this house.

ask.text: Ambrose. These two say you were supposed to find them.
Find them, sir? I'm not sure I...

count.text: Ninety-nine... one hundred. Ready or not.

found.text: Found you, Miss Frida. Miss Wilhelmina.

after.text: I seem to have lost track of the time, sir.
It happens. I hear it happens a lot here.

bedroom.text: They drew me. As a bat. Hanging in a wardrobe.

guest.text: Locked. Or stuck. Or held shut by something small.

linen.text: This one doesn't open. From this side.

fight.title: The toy army
fight.controls: Move A/D · Jump W/Space · Swipe E/J · Throw sketch F/K

phase1.text: Wind-up soldiers. I've faced worse. I've faced stairs.

clear2.text: Now you have to catch us.

won.text: Let's not get ahead of ourselves.
